Suffixed subject of the infinitive construct, realized by the English subject pronoun.
The infinitival לְ is realized by the 'of' governing the English gerund; treating 'of' as supplied by 'end' and the לְ as unrepresented is also defensible.
'his own' both realize the pronominal suffix; 'own' is the ASV's emphatic expansion of it, not an addition.
'round about' is one adverbial rendering of סָבִיב.
bamah is one noun rendered by two English words; headed on high as the word carrying the lexeme, with places the generic noun supplied to expand it (rule 31, dry land).

The ASV spends one English word, 'pleased', on the fixed idiom yatab be-eyney, so the verb and the preposition and noun of the idiom share a unit under rule 30, just as heshiv panim fuses to 'deny' beside the complement's own English word. The competing analysis reads the transitive recasting like rules 21 and 40 and leaves be- and eyney unrepresented.
The nomen rectum of eyney takes its own English words; the article of the divine title belongs to the noun that licenses it.
The frozen suffix of Adonai has no English realization.
ASV has 'this thing' without an article.
Article of agreement on the demonstrative; ASV has no second 'the'.

The ASV renders the definite demonstrative phrase as this thing, with no English the.
The article agreeing with the demonstrative has no English word; this realizes s013 alone. Fusing s012 with s013 is defensible.

'burnt' carries the lexeme of olah and 'offerings' is the generic noun supplied to expand it (rule 31); heading on 'offerings' remains defensible.
ASV renders this second asah as 'offered'.
'peace' carries the lexeme of shelem and 'offerings' is the generic noun supplied to expand it (rule 31).
